stops.info: This slice starts when an Agent sends an MCP tools/call request. The Relay validates the tool name, forwards its arguments, and converts success or failure into MCP's text result shape.
The Relay crosses the process boundary here: it discovers the target Neovim, invokes docent.rpc.dispatch over nvim_exec_lua, and retries once if that RPC channel died.
Inside the user's Neovim, this tiny dispatcher maps the MCP tool name to a function in docent.tools. pcall keeps plugin errors contained and turns them into data the Relay can return cleanly.

This is the application boundary for add_tour_stop: resolve and verify the file, validate line and Info, then pass a normalized Stop into the Tour domain. Only the first Stop returns the user's real pacing key.
The Tour owns the live state as stack frames. Adding the first Stop creates a root frame, installs the temporary escape behavior, and auto-navigates; later Stops only queue, preserving user control.
Navigation is the editor-side effect seam: reuse an existing window or edit the file, clamp the requested line, center the cursor, then delegate range highlighting and the Info float to the UI.
The UI renders a Stop's Info in a non-focusable cursor-relative float, sizes it to wrapped content, and closes it on the user's next cursor move or buffer change.
Control now passes back to the user: setup binds the configured next and previous keys only when they do not overwrite a user mapping, and records the keys so Agents report the actual pacing control.

When the user advances, next chooses the following Stop and goto_stop updates current before reusing the same navigate path. At a sub-tour boundary it pops to the parent; at the root's end it stays put and reports completion.
The E2E case locks down the whole slice: first Stop auto-jumps, later Stops do not, the configured key advances in order, and pacing past the last Stop does not move the cursor.
